item.title: Neutralized or -EX
item.content:encoded:
this could be a neutralized or explained scp, due to its "not so mysterious" nature, explained because it could be perfectly be imagined as a real life decease, due to its simplicity, or neutralized because the foundation is advanced enough to contain it, and even neutralize it (also an argument for explained). I mean, I could be wrong, tell me you agree or disagree, and why. have a nice day… night… I dunno.

EDIT:

also:

An -EX, which stands for Explained, SCP is one which we have figured out. It is an SCP that is no longer an SCP, either because it has become common place, we worked out the rules behind it, or that it has just become a complete non issue.

- Bright

These are SCPs which are no longer considered odd, paranormal, or extraordinary by current standards. They are written with this in mind.

- Content Archives

so yeah… it could be perfectly -EX

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This article is not, in and of itself, bad. The only issue is that in the new era of the Foundation, this kind of stuff isn't as unique or horrifying as it was before.

Having all of the tissues in your body fuse together is quite horrifying, but the problem with this is that it doesn't feel like a real progression at this point. I think that the effect and basic structure is fine, but ultimately, the SCP doesn't do a whole lot to build off the initial premise, leading to a somewhat mixed impact, since the climax is so early.

Some slight expansions to improve on the overall narrative flow, in order to have a bigger impact, would improve this article's base, and update it for a more modern Foundation.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hi people. I'm happy to take a crack at revamping this article if someone presents a decent idea. I haven't been active here for a while and will likely be very off-and-on so if someone wants to take ownership then you have my blessing.

I think Kalinin raises a very good point. I am a fan of the "short and sweet" SCPs but in this case I believe it's to the article's detriment.

One idea I had at the time, was that all these people who had been affected by the virus had died due to medical complications which would not have occurred had they not tried to interfere with the process of the virus. That is, if the subject submits to the virus and allows it to operate uninterrupted, their respiratory and digestive systems will remain functional even as they curl into a blob.

From there I can think of a few "stage 2" possibilities to bring this more into the realm of the Foundation:

1. subject continues morphing into some kind of slug creature. lives their life as a slug with their human memories and cognitive skills
2. subject forms into a cocoon and emerges a beautiful butterfly (or more likely some kind of horrible monster)
3. subject continues growing flesh outward from their central blob indefinitely, becoming a fixture of their environment

Just some silly top-of-the-head ideas.

It's not bad, in that there's nothing particularly wrong with it. Series 1 has a distinctive short-but-sweet style that this is emblematic of, and that can be cool a lot of the time.

Mostly, though, this doesn't strike me as something the Foundation would contain. It seems like a disease that's understandable through currently understood science. It's certainly unpleasant and would induce quite a bit of panic, but it seems a plausible (albeit exotic) real-world illness.

I'm not sure what direction I'd take this, but it needs, in my opinion, something a little extra to justify why this is the Foundation's jurisdiction, and not the WHO's.

item.title: CALL FOR REVIEW
item.content:encoded:
This is a call for review for this article.

This is one of those unusual cases for me in that I literally have no idea why this isn't much higher rated. I mean, maybe it could use a bit of polish? I don't even know, and that does not make for a good review. Let's try and dig down into what makes this SCP work, and then maybe we'll get some idea as to why it's not up there in the forties and fifties.

Well, for starters, holy crap this thing is terrifying. All your skin fuses together until you just end up as one big mass of flesh. It's similar to the Flesh Beasts, only here it's done much, much slower, and what I assume is much more painful. The fact that this is a virus just makes it more horrifying, because viruses can spread quickly and you can't tell where they are and it could happen at any time and GET IT OFF GET IT OFF GET IT OFF

Ahem. Sorry.

One thing in particular that I really like is the notable cases section. Those snippets of patient information give us so much to work with, and we can visualize each scenario playing out. The final entry is horrifying, since it does suggest that the virus can break through the placental barrier (*shudder*), but my particular favorite is the third one, about the home-made head brace. I just imagine this girl, scared out of her mind, desperately building a thing to keep her mouth from fusing together.

Normally this is the part where I would pull comments about the article, but to be honest most of the reviews here are positive. The people who have read this article tend to like it, or at least not hate it. The only recurring nitpick I see is that it reminds several people of an episode of Fringe. While I haven't seen that particular episode of Fringe, I do think that while that point might be valid, the underlying idea is one that has popped up several times in various stories (like The Matrix, or I Have No Mouth And I Must Scream).

So that's where this review sits, and I'm stumped. I think the only critique I actually have is that it would be nice for the containment procedures to detail how they're keeping the virus itself contained, and how they're handling reported cases if it's not contained (the thought terrifies me). It doesn't detract from the article, though, and that's where my confusion lies.

Some fresh eyes would help with this, I feel. Please, tell us what you think about this article, the good or the bad. Perhaps all we need is just some more visibility for this article, or maybe there's something that everyone's overlooking. Thank you for reading!
